index.php: Welcome to your main cockpit. This page summarizes your key financial figures and shows two interactive charts, built from live data in your invoices, expenses, and bank transactions.

• Total Sales: The cumulative amount from all posted invoices (draft invoices and voided invoices are excluded - a draft is not a real sale yet).
  • Total Expenses: The cumulative amount from all expenses that have not been cancelled.
  • Net Profit / Balance: Total Sales minus Total Expenses. Shown in green when positive, red when negative.

If your database has no real sales yet (under 100 kr. in total), the KPI cards and both charts show simulated demo data instead, clearly marked with an information banner. The Financial Performance chart can also show its own, separate demo note if there simply isn't any posted activity within the specific period currently selected, even while the rest of the page shows real figures.
Account Balance Trend: A line chart of your running bank balance, built from imported bank transactions. Use the dropdown to change the period (1/3/6/12 months) - the chart always ends today.
Financial Performance (Cash Flow): A bar chart of your actual posted sales and expenses, grouped into real date-bounded periods across the selected range (3/6/12 months) - not an estimate.
sales_hub.php: This central module allows you to monitor, filter, and manage all client billings and sales documents.
• Invoice Registry: Displays a searchable list of all generated invoices, including invoice numbers, issue dates, customer names, and total amounts including VAT.
• Status Tracking: Invoices are categorized by lifecycle states: Draft (editable, not yet sent), Sent (open and awaiting payment), and Paid (settled).
• Actionable Shortcuts: Click on any invoice row or number to open the editor. Use the primary controls to generate a brand new invoice, export data, or issue a credit note for returns.
Use the search parameters above the table to quickly isolate records by specific date intervals, customer names, or specific payment statuses.

Other Statuses: Invoices can also be Void (cancelled, never collected) or Credited (a credit note was issued against it) - these aren't shown as filter tabs but appear as status badges on the invoice itself.
Partial Payments: A "sent" invoice that has received a partial payment (registered via bank reconciliation) shows its remaining balance as a small "Remaining:" line under the amount.
invoice_edit.php: Here you can create or edit invoices for your customers. Follow these standard guidelines:
• Select a customer from the list to start a new invoice.
• Enter the correct invoice date and the payment due date.
• Choose a product from the dropdown menu to insert it into a line.
• The system automatically retrieves the price and VAT rate from the database.
• Quantity and price can be adjusted manually on each individual line.
• The subtotal, VAT, and grand total are calculated automatically at the bottom.
• Internal notes will not be visible on the customer's printed invoice.
• Remember to click Save Invoice to store your changes securely.

Foreign Currency: If the currency module is enabled, you can invoice in a foreign currency by entering it along with an exchange rate - the invoice displays in that currency, while your bookkeeping still converts and posts in DKK.
invoice_view.php: Here you can preview the complete invoice layout before finalizing it.
• Click Design Mode to unlock elements and customize their positions on the page.
• Drag elements around freely to adjust the visual spacing of your invoice layout.
• Resize elements by dragging their right edge to fit your official business template.
• Your changes are saved automatically to the database whenever you release an element.
• Enter a custom text in the Email Message field to personalize your digital dispatch.
• Click Send via Mail to automatically generate a PDF and email it directly to the customer.
• Use the OIOUBL XML button to export a compliant Danish e-invoice for NemHandel.
• Click Print to open the browser dialogue; all system buttons are automatically hidden on paper.
• Click Leave to safely return to the sales hub when you are finished.
Foreign Currency Invoices: If the invoice was created in a foreign currency, it displays and prints in that currency here - your bookkeeping still records the DKK-converted amount behind the scenes.

Payment History: If any payments have been registered via bank reconciliation, they are listed here along with the remaining balance - or a "Fully paid" confirmation once the full amount has been received.
setup_chart.php: This one-time setup screen lets you choose and install the initial Chart of Accounts template for a fresh installation.

• Template Choices: Choose between three templates: Simple (freelancers and service businesses without inventory), Standard (small businesses with standard VAT, vehicle, and administrative accounts), and Extended (comprehensive layout for corporations with employees, depreciation, and financial assets).
  • Locked Once In Use: If your accounts table already contains data, installation is locked to protect your existing bookkeeping - you cannot overwrite it from here.
  • Live Preview: The account list updates instantly as you select a different template, so you can review it before committing.
Review the template carefully before installing - once your accounts are in active use, changing structure later requires manual account edits instead.
customer_edit.php: This page allows you to create a new client profile or update the information of an existing customer in your database.
• Required Information: The Customer Name is mandatory to save the profile. All other details are optional but recommended for accurate invoicing.
• Company Details: Inputting the CVR (Company Registration Number) and a designated Contact Person ensures professional, correct layouts when generating financial documents.

• Payment Terms: The Payment Days field defines the default credit duration for this specific client (pre-set to 8 days). When creating a new invoice for this customer, the due date will automatically adjust based on this value.
• Internal Notes: The Notes field is strictly for internal tracking and administration. Information written here will never be visible on the customer's printed invoices.
Click Save Changes to store the modifications securely. Use the Back button to return to the Sales Hub without altering any data.
Deleting a Customer: A customer linked to existing invoices or projects cannot be deleted - remove or reassign those first if you need to delete the customer record.
bank_import_step1.php: This module helps you import financial transactions from your bank using a standard CSV file, bypassing manual ledger entry.
• Load Saved Profile: If you frequently import data from the same bank, you can select a previously saved profile from the dropdown menu to instantly restore your custom column mappings.

• Data Preview & Delimiter Auto-Detection: Uploading your CSV file displays a 6-row sample. The system automatically detects whether your file uses semicolons (;) or commas (,) as dividers, and maps out columns as Col. 1, Col. 2, etc.

• Column Mapping Fields: Provide the exact column numbers containing your data. The engine attempts to pre-fill these fields by analyzing headers for words like Date/Dato, Text/Tekst, or Amount/Beløb.
• Skip Lines: Most bank files contain a header row or meta-information at the top. Set this to 1 (or higher) to prevent the import engine from reading text headers as financial entries.
• Save Layout Profile: To avoid mapping columns manually next time, write the bank's name under Save as Profile and click the floppy disk icon (💾) to store the configuration.
Verify your configurations carefully against the preview table, then click Complete Import to transfer the structured data to the processing environment.
After Import: Completing the import sends you to Bank Reconciliation, where each imported line is matched against invoices or categorized as an expense.
reconcile_list.php: This workspace allows you to match your imported bank statement lines with your outstanding sales invoices or quickly assign operational expenses to the correct ledger accounts.

• Green Amounts (Incoming Payments): These lines represent customer payments. The engine automatically scans your system for unpaid invoices with an identical total. If a precise match is located, the invoice dropdown is highlighted in green and pre-selected for you.

• Fee Calculations (⚡ Fee): If a payment originates from a payment gateway (e.g., Stripe, MobilePay), click the ⚡ Fee link. This dynamically evaluates and applies processing fees directly into your designated fee account using your preset fixed, relative, or mixed calculation models.
• Red Amounts (Outgoing Payments): These represent card expenses, supplier payments, or transfers. Select the appropriate cost or asset account from the dropdown list to categorize the entry.

• Database Actions Upon Confirmation: When you click OK, the application handles a three-tier double-entry ledger sequence: a unique tracking id is assigned in the journal, matching balancing lines are added to your ledger, and the temporary line is flagged as permanently processed.
• Discarding Records: Click the trash icon (🗑️) to delete individual temporary lines that do not belong in your bookkeeping accounts.
Review each transaction line carefully. Once verified, hit the green action button to securely process and commit the data to your permanent accounting books.
Period Lock: Transactions dated before your accounting lock date (set in Company Settings or via Close Fiscal Year) cannot be reconciled - this protects already-closed periods from changes.

Partial Payments: If the bank amount is less than an invoice's full total, it is recorded as a partial payment - the invoice stays "sent" and its remaining balance (shown in the dropdown) shrinks accordingly. Once payments add up to the full amount, the invoice is automatically marked "paid".
settings_fees.php: This management panel allows you to automate the calculation of processing fees charged by external payment gateways or merchant accounts (such as Stripe, MobilePay, or PayPal).
• Source Name: Specify the unique identifier of the transaction provider (e.g., stripe). This value matches the transaction's import source tag when processing lines in the reconciliation system.

• Calculation Models: Choose how fees are assessed:
    • Fixed amount: Deducts a flat rate per transaction line regardless of volume.
    • Percentage: Subtracts a variable percentage based strictly on the gross sum.
    • Mixed: Combines both fixed components and dynamic percentages for high-accuracy transaction mapping.

• Rate & Fixed Rates Fields: Enter the dynamic variables used in your math calculation layouts. For percentage rates, format the amount using standard decimals (e.g., input 0.014 to map a 1.4% processing layout). For flat adjustments, define the strict numeric price value directly (e.g., 1.00).

• Active Rules Management: The lower panel displays a full directory of established configurations active in your current engine instance. Click the trash bin icon (🗑️) to permanently erase redundant rules from the master system settings.
Click Save Rule to instantly commit changes. Once logged, the rules are instantly reachable inside your live reconciliation workspace via the lightning bolt trigger tool.
inventory_status.php: This dashboard provides a complete real-time directory of your product catalog, tracking active stock volumes, current price structures, and financial mapping.
• SKU & Identification: The SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) column displays your unique identifier. If no custom SKU is specified for a product, the core system identifier (ID) is used automatically.

• Account Mapping: The Account column specifies which financial account inside your chart of accounts receives the turnover when this product is added to a sales invoice. If a product shows No account, it should be updated immediately to secure precise double-entry layouts.
• Pricing & Currency: Prices are rendered automatically based on your system configuration preferences (e.g., DKK or EUR) and match the baseline layout defined on the product setup page.

• Data Management & Export: Use the top-right toolbar buttons to interact with your data catalog: click New Product (➕) to expand your collection, or use CSV to generate a clean raw spreadsheet export of your current stock directory.
• Modifying Records: Click the pencil icon (📝) in the actions column to jump directly to the modification workspace for that individual line.
Review your product rows regularly to verify your active stock balances remain fully aligned with your physical asset tracking workflows.
product_edit.php: This form allows you to create a new product item or update the details, pricing, and stock thresholds of an existing catalog record.

• Sales Price & Netto Input: Enter the baseline sales price excluding VAT. The system handles both comma (,) and dot (.) notation entries automatically.
  • Account Mapping: Select the account this product's sales should post to, from your full chart of accounts. Choosing an account with a VAT code attached determines the VAT rate applied to this product.
  • Dynamic Gross Pricing (Price incl. VAT): The lower summary panel calculates and displays the final customer retail price in real-time, based on your netto input and the selected account's VAT rate.
  • Stock Tracking & Warning Thresholds:
    • In Stock: The current physical quantity available.
    • Min. Level: The critical stock boundary - when inventory drops to or below this, automated warning indicators appear across your dashboard.
Click Save Changes or Create Product to submit. Use Cancel to discard edits and return to the inventory overview.
expense_list.php: This workspace serves as a centralized log for tracking and managing all operational expenditures, supplier purchases, and digital financial receipts.

• Supplier & Category Tracking: Each line isolates the exact business supplier alongside a brief description. The Account column verifies which specific operating or asset account from your chart of accounts has been impacted by the entry.

• Smart Attachment Indicators: The File column identifies linked vouchers or documentation using unique markers:
    • Paperclip (📎): Indicates a standard external file attachment (e.g., uploaded receipt or picture).
    • Invoice-Dollar Icon (): Identifies internal generated voucher files managed securely within your system layout.
    • Three dashes (---): Signals that no digital document copy is assigned to this expense row.
• Expanding the Log: Click the Add Expense button (➕) in the upper-right control field to switch directly to the creation layout module.
• Actions Row: Use the action triggers to modify or delete items. Clicking the trash icon prompts a defensive safety verification alert before executing any removal sequence in the data engine.
Regularly monitor this index grid to ensure your documented proofs are complete, accounts are accurately mapped, and outlays match your cash outflows.
ledger_view.php: This screen provides a full audit trail of your bookkeeping, grouped by journal entry.

• Journal Grouping (#): Multiple lines sharing the same Journal # belong to the same double-entry transaction.
  • Voucher Number: Present once an entry is posted (assigned automatically by the system, part of the gapless voucher numbering). A posted entry with a voucher number can no longer be edited or deleted directly.
  • Debit vs. Credit: Debit amounts are shown in green, credit amounts in red.
  • Cancelling an Entry: The trash icon on a journal's header row cancels it with a proper reversal entry rather than deleting it - both the original and the reversal stay visible (shown struck-through), preserving the audit trail.
Use this table to track down accounting anomalies, verify balancing, and keep your double-entry books fully auditable.
vat_report.php: This report shows the VAT payable or receivable for a selected period, calculated from your actual bookkeeping - not recalculated from account rates.

• Period Selection: Choose a year and, if needed, narrow it down to a specific month, quarter, or half-year - the actual reporting periods used by most Danish businesses when filing with SKAT.
  • Sales VAT / Purchase VAT: These figures are read directly from the amounts actually posted to your configured VAT accounts (set in Company Settings), not recalculated from a percentage rate. This ensures the report always matches your real ledger, even when a specific posting used a different VAT rate than its account's default (e.g. a VAT-exempt purchase on an otherwise 25% account).
  • VAT Payable: Sales VAT minus Purchase VAT, rounded to whole DKK as required by SKAT's TastSelv Erhverv. This is the figure to report.
  • Breakdown Table: Shows net amounts grouped by VAT code, for reference and cross-checking only - the headline figures above are the ones that count.
If any figures look wrong, check that your accounts have the correct VAT code assigned in the Chart of Accounts.
report_income.php: This report compiles your official income statement and a precise VAT settlement, calculated directly from your posted bookkeeping (journal and ledger) - not from invoice or expense records directly.

• Revenue: The total of all posted income-account entries (double-entry bookkeeping), regardless of invoice status - this reflects your actual accounting, not just paid invoices.
  • Costs: Grouped by the individual expense account they were posted to, taken directly from your ledger.
  • Annual Result: Revenue minus Total Costs, shown in green for a surplus and red for a deficit.
  • Precise VAT Statement: Sales VAT Due and Deductible Purchase VAT are read from your two configured VAT accounts (set in Company Settings), giving you the net VAT to pay or receive.
This report sums your entire bookkeeping across all dates. For a specific fiscal year only, use Close Fiscal Year instead.
chart_of_accounts.php: This master register controls your organization's financial structure. Every posting in the journal and ledger is tied to one of these accounts.

• VAT Code & Rate: Shows the tax code and rate inherited from the linked VAT code. Accounts with no VAT code show "-".
  • Special Accounts: Accounts configured in Company Settings for automatic postings (Bank, Debtors, Sales, Output VAT, Input VAT) are highlighted with a colored badge. Rename or delete these with care - change the role in Company Settings first, not here.
  • Adding & Editing: Click Add New Account to create a new account. Use the row actions to edit or delete an existing one.
Modify your accounts with care - structural changes affect how transactions populate your journal, ledger, and financial reports.
company_settings.php: This page controls your company profile, banking details, default accounts, and system-wide preferences.

• Company Details: Your legal name, address, CVR number, and contact info - used on invoices and in the annual report.
  • Banking: Your bank registration and account number, shown on invoices to help customers pay you correctly.
  • Default Accounts: Choose which accounts in your chart of accounts should automatically receive bank, debtor, sales, and VAT postings. Changing these affects all future automatic postings.
  • Date Format & Currency: Sets how dates are displayed throughout the system and your primary business currency. Changing currency can affect how historical data is displayed.
  • Default Mail Body: The standard text used when emailing invoices to customers, unless overridden per invoice.
  • SAF-T Export: Exports your complete bookkeeping in the standardized SAF-T format for tax audits.
Review your changes carefully before saving - these settings affect invoices, reports, and automatic postings across the whole system.
about.php: This page shows basic information about your TinyCash installation and a quick system health check.

• Version & System Status: Shows the running app version, PHP version, web server, database engine, and current language.
  • Security Lock Check: Verifies that core files (like your database configuration) are properly blocked from direct web access via .htaccess. A red warning here means your server may not be enforcing these protections - check your server configuration.
  • Recent Error (admins only): If an error was logged within the last 24 hours, a short summary is shown here with the full message available on hover - useful for spotting problems quickly without digging through log files.
If the security check shows a warning on a live server, treat it as urgent and verify your .htaccess files are active.
backup.php: According to bookkeeping regulations, financial data and digital receipts must be secured outside the primary server host environment. Execute this manual verification minimum once a month:
• Download the full archive ZIP file to your local computer using the interface above.
• Upload the ZIP file to your off-site corporate remote storage (e.g., OneDrive, Jottacloud, or pCloud).
How to Verify the File Inside Your Cloud (OneDrive / Jottacloud):
• Size Matching: Open your cloud storage drive interface and locate the uploaded file. Ensure that the byte-size listed in OneDrive/Jottacloud matches the size recorded by the system above.

• Transfer Validation: If your cloud provider or operating system tools display file properties, confirm that the cloud checksum matches the unique Local MD5 token printed above. This mathematically guarantees zero data loss during upload.
• Status Check: Confirm that the remote file has finished syncing completely and displays a permanent cloud confirmation mark.
error_log.php: When the system exhibits unexpected behavior, locked UI elements, or missing layout buttons, the root cause is recorded in the server logs. Debugging requires cross-referencing these three distinct environments:

• System Error Log (PHP Error Log): Catches critical backend server errors (e.g., Fatal Error: Call to undefined function lang()). If a page stops rendering mid-execution, crashes, or displays a blank white screen, the exact file name and PHP line number are logged here. How to view: You are viewing this log directly on this page (error_log.php).

• Apache Access Log: Records all incoming HTTP network requests in real-time. Use this to verify if the browser's asynchronous AJAX calls are successfully reaching the server, and to check the exact response code returned. How to view: Accessed through your web hosting control panel (e.g., cPanel/Plesk under 'Logs') or via FTP/SSH at /var/log/apache2/access.log.

• Browser Console (F12): Captures client-side errors executing directly in the user's browser (e.g., JavaScript ReferenceError: isNotepadMaximized is not defined). If a modal cannot be dragged or a button click fails without reloading the page, check this log. How to view: Right-click anywhere on this webpage, select 'Inspect', and click on the 'Console' tab.
How to Interpret Status Codes in the Access Log / Network Tab:
• Status 200 (OK): The request was successful, and data was exchanged correctly (e.g., when the notepad script outputs 'saved').
• Status 403 (Forbidden): Access denied. Typically triggered by strict security rules in your .htaccess file or because your PHP session (auth.inc.php) rejected the request due to a timeout.
• Status 404 (Not Found): The file path is incorrect. This happens if a script attempts to invoke an include file from a non-existent directory or using an incorrect filename.

• Status 500/503 (Internal Error): The server crashed during script execution. This always indicates a fatal PHP code failure, and the exact error description must be retrieved from the server's PHP Error Log.
Note: When modifying source files, always force a hard browser reload (Ctrl + F5 or Cmd + Shift + R) to clear old, cached JavaScript logic from the browser's local memory.
login.php: This entry gateway acts as the primary firewall for the application ecosystem, managing user session validation, defensive runtime audits, and persistent telemetry tracking.

• First-Run Installation Check (Setup Intercept): Upon initialization, the core routine executes an automated query to evaluate row counts inside the central users data array. If the lookup catches a flat result zero (0) and detects the presence of the system deployment block (inc/user_create_admin.php), the execution automatically re-routes traffic to the default setup layout.

• Defensive Parametric Queries: Inbound credential checks avoid raw injection vulnerabilities by routing verification parameters explicitly through standard prepared database templates (mysqli_prepare). Usernames are validated safely via parameterized strings before internal logic executes hash evaluations.

• Cryptographic Hash Integrity: Raw client password entries are never stored or compared in plain text. Instead, they pass through a one-way secure cryptographic verification process (password_verify) matched directly up against the recorded database hash strings.

• Audit Logging Matrix (Telemetry): Every unique authentication interaction logs persistent metadata into the central login_log index. The routing engine dynamically records the client network vector (REMOTE_ADDR), environmental software fingerprints (HTTP_USER_AGENT), and the outcome status flag (Success or Failed) to simplify security audits.

• Session Security Optimization: Following a successful credentials match, the authentication engine calls an instantaneous id regeneration procedure (session_regenerate_id(true)). This cycle invalidates the legacy session profile context immediately, neutralizing session-fixation attacks before populating global permission variables.

• Dynamic Interface Scripts: A post-rendering DOM script monitors user field configurations (#pwd_inside). It dynamically injects an absolute-positioned visibility icon (👁️) into the field parent frame, creating a secure client-side mechanism to switch input masks smoothly between hidden passwords and readable plain text strings.
Treat credentials management attentively. Ensure fallback installation files are automatically purged or locked on production systems following deployment to prevent external unauthorized access.
expense_edit.php: This screen allows you to record or edit an operational expense. You can use the Document Depot on the left to view and attach files while typing, or upload a file directly.

• Voucher Number: Assigned automatically by the system when you save a posted expense - part of the gapless, legally required voucher numbering. You don't need to enter it manually.
  • Attachment Required Above a Threshold: If the amount is at or above your configured attachment limit (set in Company Settings, default 500 kr), a receipt or document is required before you can save. Below the limit, you may save without one, but must state a short reason.
  • Document Depot: Click any file in the left column to preview it, then click Attach to link it to this expense. Files arrive here from scanners, email, or mobile photo capture, depending on what's configured.
  • AI Document Scanning: If enabled, uploading a receipt image or PDF (including scanned, image-only PDFs) can automatically pre-fill the supplier, date, and amount fields.
  • Posted Expenses Are Locked: Once an expense has been posted (has a voucher number and journal entries), its core fields can no longer be edited or deleted, in line with bookkeeping law - it can only be cancelled with a reversal entry.
Saving creates the matching double-entry journal postings automatically and moves the attached file to permanent storage.
user_list.php: This page lists all user accounts and lets administrators manage who has access to TinyCash.

• Roles: Admins are shown with a distinct badge. Roles are Administrator (full access), User (day-to-day access), and Accountant (settable when editing an existing user).
  • Edit / Delete: Use the row actions to edit a user's details or remove their account. You cannot delete or downgrade your own account, to prevent accidentally locking yourself out.
  • New User: Click New User to create another account.
Only administrators can see and use this page.
backup_restore.php: The restore form on this page only handles data backups: it overwrites the database and restores your settings and uploaded attachments from a TinyCash ZIP created with "Full Data Archive" or "System Configuration".
Restoring overwrites all current data and cannot be undone. Make sure you have a fresh backup of the current state before proceeding.

Automatic Safety Copy: Before restoring, the system automatically saves a copy of your current database to the backups/ folder (pre_restore_safety_*.sql), so you have a way back if the restore was a mistake.
The Backup Must Match the Database Engine

A backup created on SQLite cannot be restored into MySQL, or vice versa - the SQL dialects are not compatible. If the engines differ, the restore is aborted before anything is changed. Switch the active engine to match the backup, then try again.
A program backup (the application code) - and the program/ folder inside a combined weekly auto-backup - is restored manually, because overwriting live PHP files through the browser is unsafe:

1. Download and unzip the file on your own computer.
  2. Copy the program files over the project folder on the server (via SFTP or your host's file manager), replacing the old code.
  3. Do not overwrite inc/data/env.ini - it is deliberately excluded from the backup. Keep the server's own env.ini so your database and mail settings are preserved.
  4. If the database structure has changed, import program/schema.sql - but only into an empty or new database, as it contains structure without your bookkeeping data.
  5. Never copy program files into your live data folders (uploads/, data/, backups/); they are not part of a program backup.
Tip: test a program rollback on a separate host first, just as you would test any backup.
program_backup.php: Take this before and after a program update - when PHP files or the database structure change. It archives the program code (PHP and configuration files) plus the database's structure, so you can roll back code and schema if an update goes wrong.
For your security, the archive never contains:
• Your accounting data - uploads/, the database file and storage/.
Use a Full Data Archive for the accounting data - the two backups complement each other.

When the automatic weekly off-site backup runs, this program backup is automatically included under a program/ folder, so the scheduled backup is one combined archive of both your data and your program.
year_end_close.php: This closes a fiscal year: it zeroes out your income and expense accounts and transfers the net result to a chosen equity account, in one balanced journal entry.

• Preview First: The page shows a preview of the year's result before anything is posted - review it carefully.
  • Equity Account: Choose which equity account should receive the net result. Only accounts of type "Equity" are listed.
  • Locks the Period: Closing a year moves the accounting lock date forward, preventing further postings before that date - part of Danish bookkeeping law compliance. It cannot be moved backward.
  • Invoice/Voucher Numbers Are Unaffected: Numbering sequences continue unbroken across the year change, as required by law.
This is irreversible. Only administrators can close a fiscal year - make sure all transactions for the period are posted first.
annual_report.php: This page compiles a draft annual report (balance sheet, income statement, and notes) for a selected fiscal year, in one printable A4 layout with PDF download.

• Draft Only: This document is a draft, not a filing. Official annual reports for companies must be submitted digitally via XBRL through virk.dk, not as a PDF - use this as a starting point for that process or for your accountant.
  • Accounting Policy Note: A free-text note describing your accounting principles, editable and saved per installation.
  • Fiscal Year Selection: Choose which fiscal year to report on from the dropdown - only years registered under Close Fiscal Year are available.
Aimed at regnskabsklasse B (small companies) - management review is intentionally omitted, as it's exempt for this class.
balance_sheet.php: This shows a snapshot statement of your Assets, Liabilities, and Equity as of a chosen date, calculated directly from your bookkeeping.

• Status as of: Pick any date - the balance sheet recalculates for that exact point in time.
  • Balance Check: A green message confirms Assets equal Liabilities + Equity. A red warning means something was posted outside the normal flows and needs investigation.
  • Draft Only: Like the Annual Report, this is a draft for internal review or your accountant - not suitable for direct filing.
Use this to spot-check your bookkeeping's health at any point during the year, not just at year-end.
vat_codes.php: This page manages the VAT codes available when setting up accounts in your Chart of Accounts.

• ID: A short code (e.g. S25 for 25% sales VAT) used to identify this VAT rate elsewhere in the system.
  • Rate: The VAT percentage this code represents.
  • Account: Optionally link this VAT code to a specific account for reference.
Click the trash icon to delete a code that is no longer needed. Note that the actual VAT accounts used for reporting are set separately, under Company Settings.
project_view.php: This page lists all your projects and, when you open one, shows its financial detail: linked expenses, other income, and invoices.

• Project List: Shows code, customer, status, start/end dates, and a running balance (income minus expenses) for each project.
  • Project Detail: Click a project to see its individual expense, income, and invoice lines, plus the overall balance.
  • Requires the Project Module: Enable it from the New/Edit Project page to show the Project Code field on expense and invoice forms.
Use this to track profitability per project or per customer engagement, not just overall.
project_edit.php: This form creates a new project or edits an existing one.

• Project Code: A required, unique identifier for the project - used to tag expenses and invoices to it.
  • Client: Optionally link the project to a specific customer.
  • Start/End Date: Optional dates shown in reports and the project overview.
  • Invoice Concept: A suggested invoicing text you can reuse when billing this project.
  • Project Module Toggle: A separate card at the top lets you activate or deactivate the whole Project module, which controls whether the Project Code field appears on expense and invoice forms.
Deleting a project cannot be undone - it does not delete its linked expenses or invoices, only the project record itself.
account_edit.php: This form creates a new account or edits an existing one in your Chart of Accounts.

• Account Number: Cannot be changed once created - it's the account's permanent identifier used throughout the ledger.
  • Account Type: Determines how the account behaves in reports and postings: Income, Expense, Bank/Cash, VAT, Asset, Liability, or Equity. Choosing the wrong type can misclassify your reports.
  • Standard Account Mapping: Optionally link this account to a standard reference category, used for aggregated tax/statistical reporting.
  • VAT Code & Rate: Attach a VAT code from your existing codes (or type a new one) to automatically apply that VAT rate on postings to this account.
Special accounts used for automatic postings (Bank, Debtors, Sales, VAT) are configured separately in Company Settings - editing them here only changes their name/type, not their special role.
user_create.php: This form creates a new user account for TinyCash.

• Username & Password: Choose a unique username; the password is hashed securely and never stored or shown in plain text.
  • Role: Administrator has full access, including user management and system settings. User has ordinary day-to-day access. Grant admin only to trusted people.
Only administrators can create new user accounts.
user_edit.php: This form edits an existing user's username, role, and password.

• Role: Changes take effect on the user's next login. Be careful when changing your own role - you could lock yourself out of admin functions.
  • Change Password: Leave both password fields empty to keep the current password unchanged. Fill them in (matching) to set a new one.
Only administrators can edit other users' accounts.
Roles Available: Administrator (full access), User (day-to-day access), and Accountant (view/reporting-oriented access) - Accountant can only be assigned here, not at account creation.
mail_inbox.php: This page reads incoming mail directly from configured mailboxes, so you can process attachments without leaving TinyCash.

• Three Mailboxes: Switch between Vouchers & Receipts, Supplier Invoices, and Invoice Copies (Sales) - each reads a separately configured mailbox.
  • Attachments: Click an attachment to preview it, or download it directly.
  • Quick Register: In the Vouchers/Supplier mailboxes, click Register on an attachment to jump straight to a new expense with that document attached.
Mailbox credentials are configured in your server's env.ini - contact your administrator if a mailbox fails to load.
storage_browser.php: This page lets you browse, preview, download, and delete files across the system's storage folders (invoices, e-invoices, uploads, backups, and more).

• Folder Selector: Switch between the different storage areas using the sidebar.
  • Preview: Click a file to preview PDFs, images, and text files directly in the browser.
  • Deletion is Restricted for Bookkeeping Reasons: A file that is the attachment of a posted expense cannot be deleted here, in line with the legal retention requirement - even if you try from this page instead of the expense itself.
Use this for general file management and cleanup - not for touching bookkeeping attachments, which are protected by design.
audit_log.php: This page shows a read-only trail of sensitive actions - cancellations, deletions, and postings - across the system: who did it, when, and exactly what changed.

• Filters: Narrow the list by action, table, user, or date range - combine as many as you need.
  • Details: Hover the underlined text in the Details column to see the full before/after values as recorded at the time.
  • Not Everything Is Logged: Only specific sensitive actions write to this log (e.g. cancelling an expense, posting an invoice, deleting a journal entry) - it is not a complete activity log of every click.
Only administrators can see this page, since entries may include details from other users' records.
reminders.php: This page lists posted invoices (status "sent") whose due date has passed and that are not yet marked paid.

• Days Overdue: Shown in orange after 7 days and red after 14 - a quick visual sense of how urgent each one is.
  • Send Reminder: Emails the customer directly using their invoice contact address, with the amount, due date, and days overdue filled in automatically.
  • Last Reminder: Shows when a reminder was last sent for this invoice and how many times - so you can see at a glance who has already been reminded.
Only invoices with a real due date and "sent" status appear here - drafts and already-paid invoices are excluded automatically.
customer_statement.php: Account Statement: A chronological list of this customer's posted invoices and registered payments, with a running balance - the classic "kontoudtog" view. Draft invoices are not shown, since they are not yet real transactions.
Each invoice increases the balance (what the customer owes); each payment decreases it. Credit notes are shown as negative invoices, since they are stored with negative line amounts.

Period filter: Narrowing the date range does not change the running balance calculation - an "Opening Balance" row shows what was owed just before the selected period started, so the numbers always stay correct.
Use the CSV export button on the table, or the Print button, to save or hand out a copy of the statement.
recurring_invoices.php: Recurring Invoices: Templates for invoices that repeat automatically - e.g. monthly rent, a subscription, or a fixed retainer. Each template has a customer, a repeat interval (monthly/quarterly/yearly), and its own invoice lines.

A new draft invoice is generated automatically once the scheduled date arrives - it is checked on every page you visit while logged in (there is no real background scheduler on typical web hosting). The draft is never posted automatically; you still review and post it yourself, exactly like any manually created invoice.
Use Generate Now to create the next invoice immediately, without waiting for the scheduled date. Use Pause to temporarily stop a template from generating invoices, without deleting it.
recurring_invoice_edit.php: Recurring Invoice Template: Set the customer, repeat interval and next run date, plus the invoice lines that will be copied into each generated draft.

Payment Days is filled in automatically from the customer's own payment terms when you select them, but can be changed for this template alone. Foreign currency is not supported for recurring invoices - generated drafts are always in DKK.
bank_integration.php: Bank Integration (PSD2): Connects TinyCash directly to your bank via Enable Banking (Open Banking) - an alternative to manually exporting and importing a CSV file. Requires an Enable Banking account and API keys configured in inc/data/env.ini. (GoCardless, previously used here, stopped accepting new signups in July 2025.)
Connecting a bank sends you to your bank's own login page to give consent - TinyCash never sees your online banking password, only read-only account/transaction data once you approve it.
Sync Now fetches recent transactions and drops them into the same queue used by CSV import - open Bank Reconciliation afterward to match and post them, exactly as with a manual import.
Access is granted by your bank for a limited period - when it expires, the connection shows as "Expired" and needs to be reconnected.

Note: Enable Banking's pricing for real production use is not published and requires contacting their sales team - an application and sandbox can be created without a sales conversation, so you can test the connection flow before committing.
my_2fa.php: Two-Factor Login (2FA): Adds a second step at login - after your password, you also enter a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password, Bitwarden, etc.). This is per-account: each user turns it on for themselves, it cannot be turned on for someone else.

When you enable it, you are shown a secret key to enter manually in your app (no QR code - manual entry is fully supported by every authenticator app and avoids relying on a third-party service to generate an image containing your secret). You then confirm with a real code from the app before 2FA is actually switched on, so you can never lock yourself out by mis-typing the key.
Recovery codes are shown once when you enable 2FA (or regenerate them) - each can be used instead of an app code, one time only, if you lose access to your phone. Store them somewhere safe.
Disabling 2FA, or generating new recovery codes, requires re-entering your password - this stops someone with a hijacked but unattended session from turning off your account's protection.
run_migrate.php: Database Migration: Lists every known database migration script and checks live whether each has already been applied to this specific installation - "Applied" or "Pending".

All migrations are idempotent (safe to run more than once - a migration that already ran will simply report "already exists" and do nothing). Clicking "Run now" / "Run again" opens the individual migration script in a new tab; reload this page afterward to see its status update.

This page does not run everything in one click by design - each migration script has its own independent result page, so you can see exactly what happened for each one rather than one combined, harder-to-read log.
menu_visibility.php: Menu Visibility: A full list of every menu item, with a checkbox per user level (1 Beginner, 2 Experienced, 3 Developer) controlling whether it shows in the menu for that level.

This is a declutter tool, not access control. Hiding an item here only removes it from the menu - it does not stop someone typing the page's address directly, unless the page itself also has its own access restriction for that level. Use it to keep the menu simple for beginners, not to protect sensitive pages.
Items with no saved row use the original built-in defaults (shown pre-filled). Reset All to Defaults clears every saved setting and returns to those built-in defaults.
